newsitem.title: USA: Miller will appeal fired exec's $26 mln award.
newsitem.headline: Miller will appeal fired exec's $26 mln award.

text.p: A former executive at Miller Brewing Co. who claimed he was unjustly fired for telling a co-worker about a racy "Seinfeld" episode was "overwhelmed" by a $26.6 million jury award, his lawyer said Wednesday.

Lawyers for Miller Brewing Co. said they would appeal Tuesday's jury award to Jerold Mackenzie, a former $95,000-per-year executive fired in 1993. Mackenzie said in his lawsuit that the stigma of the sexual harassment allegation had prevented him from landing a job.
"He's overwhelmed" with the Milwaukee County jury's verdict, Mackenzie's lawyer Bridget Boyle said.
Mackenzie, 54, had asked for $9 million, based on what his earnings would have been if he had not been passed over for promotion to a director's post and had worked until he was 65.

The award, much of it for punitive damages, included $24.5 million against Miller, a unit of Philip Morris Companies Inc.; $1.5 million against Mackenzie's female colleague and accuser Patricia Best, and $601,500 against Miller executive Robert Smith.

Mackenzie testified that he asked Best if she had watched the previous night's Seinfeld episode, in which the comedian's character cannot remember his girlfriend's name but knows it rhymes with a female body part.
Although she had not seen the show and expressed little interest, Mackenzie showed Best a page from the dictionary with the word for the body part. The girlfriend's name was Dolores.
Mackenzie had previously been passed over for promotion at Miller, and he alleged the company used the harassment charge as an excuse to fire him.
